observed_selected_catalog_entry.title: Derive and falsify bounded error-correcting codes

environment.language: ISO C17 implementation; exact final C17/C23 source access remains distinct from mathematical coding proof
environment.target: Hosted Linux x86-64; strict Cortex-M4 object/link audit only
environment.dependencies: Original arithmetic/bit encoder, decoder and interleave; hosted independent oracle separate from target runtime

passages: Section3, printed150-153: checking number, power-of-two check positions and seven-position construction
Section4, printed153-154: overall even parity and0/1/2-error cases
Section5, printed154-155: distance and TableV detection/correction bounds

limitations: Six native C17 profiles and four strict target object/link audits passed; no target execution or physical channel evidence.
Finite tests and mathematical model premises are not absolute mastery.
No cryptographic authenticity, insertion/deletion correction or unbounded burst guarantee.

objective_coverage.assessed_claim: Representation, parity derivation and code distance: Derive check positions, injectivity, minimum distance4 and both payload widths.; Bounded decoder and failure publication: Correct every admitted single flip, detect double flips, preserve refusal output and reject unsupported bounds.; Higher-error and attacker counterexamples: Demonstrate miscorrection, valid-word forgery and wrong-phase identity; separate noise correction from authenticity and real channel behavior.
Burst interleaving, phase and costs: Implement four-lane and rotating-phase maps, derive burst bounds and compare rate/work/buffering under equal guarantees.
Erasure recovery and independent nearest-codeword oracle: Derive2t+s<4, construct the enumerative recovery, compare independent codebooks and explain finite coverage.

rubric.criterion: Representation, parity derivation and code distance: Derive check positions, injectivity, minimum distance4 and both payload widths.

levels.3: Independently derives and verifies the changed erasure/phase assumption after the recorded delay.
